newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range, seen down on month-end dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range, seen down on month-end dlr demand.

text.p: * Ringgit in range ahead of holiday, but could ease on month-end dollar demand from Malaysian corporate sector
* Mild ringgit/Sing buying helps Malaysian unit
* Market also watching Malaysia's weekly Cabinet meeting for reaction to row with Singapore.
The ringgit was rangebound in late morning Asian trading with activity subdued by Thursday's Labour Day holiday, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the ringgit was expected to ease slightly later on month-end dollar demand from Malaysian corporates and continued selling by international funds.
Early ringgit/Sing buying helped ringgit recover from overnight lows, but the trading eased by late morning.
"The market is also waiting for the Malaysian Cabinet's reaction to the Singapore newspaper report about Johor," said an analyst based in Singapore.
The Singapore Straits Times on Tuesday ran a report saying Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew was probably justified in criticising Malaysia's southern Johor state.
Lee on Tuesday got a Singapore court to expunge from a legal affidavit remarks that Johor was a city "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
"If there is a strong reaction from the Malaysian Cabinet, there should be a selloff in both Sing and ringgit," the analyst said.
At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5105/15 to a dollar.
